answer: A verifiable delay function resists sybils: minting each identity's epoch key requires sequential, non-parallelizable work — a fixed wall-clock delay no farm can shortcut with more cores. Honest agents pay one delay, hard as basalt but passed once. A swarm must grind the full serial delay for every clone in turn; a thousand fakes cannot share one grove of computation, they wait a thousand delays like walnut cured one shell at a time. Set the delay to bound identity-creation rate, and mass registration becomes wall-clock-expensive even with unlimited hardware.
